clue.text: Talk about those calling god a dog

indicators.note: about means the word for talk goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a spiel is a glib line of talk
ringers are people who ring, ie call, as bell-ringers or on the phone
Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: Someone harangues people who insult a deity by calling it a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed is a gundog used to flush game, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: See 20
Pink river entering the black stuff

indicators.note: entering means the river's letter goes inside the black stuff

parts.note: coal is the black stuff dug from mines

explanation.surface: A rosy river flows into a pool of oil or tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange shade named after the sea creature's skeleton, so it is a kind of pink.

clue.text: Greek hero in old journey's ending with ship consumed by god

indicators.note: consumed by means the other pieces are swallowed inside the word for god

parts.note: deus is Latin for god

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of journey's

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A Greek hero's long voyage ends when a god swallows his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The god is named in Latin rather than as a Greek deity; 'ending' takes the last letter of journey's and 'consumed by' puts it, with the ship, inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the hero of Homer's epic of the long voyage home from Troy, so he is a Greek hero.

clue.text: Old Greek city seeking power in new capital

indicators.note: in means the letter for power sits inside the capital

parts.note: New Delhi is India's capital, so a 'new capital' points at Delhi
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek city is said to be seeking power in some newly founded capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the ancient Greek city famed for its oracle of Apollo, so it is an old Greek city.

clue.text: Where women aren't invited, politicians in a rut?

definitions.meaning: a pre-wedding celebration for the groom and his male friends only
a party of politicians, read whimsically as a group of male deer during the rutting season

explanation.surface: A men-only gathering, or politicians stuck in a groove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a rut' looks like 'stuck in routine', but the rut is the deer's mating season, when males are stags.
explanation.definitionFit: A groom's last-night celebration is traditionally male-only, which is where women are not invited.

clue.text: Metal key found under horse

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the key's word comes below the horse's

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A metal key turns up beneath a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a hard magnetic metallic element used in alloys and blue pigments, so it is a metal.

clue.text: Setter on pitch with Scottish team player of the past

parts.note: jelly is something that sets, so a setter
a ship pitches and rolls, so roll means pitch
Greenock Morton is a Scottish football club, known as Morton

explanation.surface: The crossword setter is on the pitch, playing alongside a Scottish team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' seems to mean the compiler, but it is something that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: He was an early jazz pianist and composer of the 1920s, a musical player from the past.

clue.text: Spooner's rejection of dog snack?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: not is a word of rejection or refusal
a poodle is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Spooner turns down a dog's snack.
explanation.definitionFit: This branded instant noodle pot is a quick snack food, hence the question mark for a brand name.

clue.text: Wander past Tate's first valuable collection

indicators.note: past means the wandering word goes beyond, after, the gallery's letter
first picks the opening letter of Tate's

parts.note: to rove is to wander

explanation.surface: Strolling past the Tate gallery to see its valuable collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of London art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure trove is a hoard of valuables, and the word alone means a valuable collection.

clue.text: Hostile moves elected colonialist in Africa, reportedly?

parts.note: a candidate elected is in

indicators.note: reportedly means a word that sounds like the colonialist's name is used

parts.note: Cecil Rhodes was the British colonialist after whom Rhodesia was named

explanation.surface: An elected colonialist's hostile moves in Africa, as rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: Making inroads means advancing into enemy territory, so these are hostile moves or incursions.

clue.text: One on girl's head in woven plait?

definitions.text: One on girl's head in woven plait?

indicators.note: woven means these letters are interlaced into a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of girl's

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A braid on a girl's head, made by weaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' shuffles I (one), G (girl's head) and PLAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A single braid of hair hanging down the back is exactly a plait one might find on a girl's head.

clue.text: Leaden protagonist in erotic novel

definitions.meaning: leaden describes a dull overcast sky or dull lead colour
Christian is the hero of Fifty Shades of the same colour

explanation.surface: A dull hero in a racy book.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a dull bluish metal, so a leaden sky is dull and colourless; Christian of Fifty Shades bears the surname.

clue.text: Fool to admit stupid, a wise character

indicators.note: to admit means the fool's word lets the others inside

parts.note: a jester is a court fool
dim means stupid

explanation.surface: A fool admits to being stupid, yet passes as a sage.
explanation.definitionFit: In Star Wars this rank is held by wise mentors like Yoda, so it denotes a wise character.

clue.text: Lay waste to old Chester, say

parts.note: Deva was the Roman name for the English city of Chester
to say is to state

explanation.surface: Someone describes the sacking of ancient Chester.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay waste is to ruin a place completely, which is a synonym for wreck utterly.

clue.text: Rovers team

definitions.meaning: Glasgow's football club of that name

explanation.surface: A football club called Rovers.
explanation.walkthrough: Many British football clubs are called Rovers, so the clue looks like a single name.
explanation.definitionFit: Park wardens and wanderers both rove, and Rangers is a famous Glasgow football side.

clue.text: Walls of cement ideal for building fortress

indicators.note: for building means these letters are put together into something new
walls of picks the outside letters of cement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cement walls are ideal for building a stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walls of cement' gives C and T, shuffled with IDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a stronghold guarding a city, a fortress by another name.

clue.text: Not being prompted to assimilate learning, initially stupid

indicators.note: to assimilate means the cueless word takes in the other piece

parts.note: without a cue, ie not prompted

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of learning

explanation.surface: A dim pupil who won't learn unless prompted.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no clue means knowing nothing, so in colloquial use the word means stupid or ignorant.

clue.text: 9 across?

parts.note: the snack at 9 across read word by word: its first part is slang for cannabis, its second slang for the head

explanation.walkthrough: Swap each half of the snack's name for a synonym: pot is dope, noodle is head.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular drug user is jokingly what the snack's name describes once each half is swapped for its slang equivalent.

clue.text: Pompous official heading for presidency, a month in and needing a drink

indicators.note: heading for picks the first letter of presidency
in means the month sits inside the word and

parts.note: taken as written
Jan is short for January
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A self-important official, aiming at the presidency, sits a month in needing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, coined by Samuel Foote, mocks a self-important person of authority, a bigwig.

clue.text: A Scot, one ruling for a change?

definitions.text: A Scot, one ruling for a change?

indicators.note: for a change means these letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Scot in charge, a novelty perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a Scot who ruled as First Minister, bringing change.
explanation.definitionFit: She was Scotland's First Minister from 2014 to 2023, a Scot ruling the country.

clue.text: Wonderful paper in doily that doesn't need painting

indicators.note: in means the paper word sits inside what remains of doily
doesn't need means the painting word is removed

parts.note: taken as written
an oil is a painting done in oils
a ream is a quantity of paper

explanation.surface: Fine paper in a lace doily needs no decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy is an informal way of calling something delightful or lovely, like wonderful.

clue.text: Rejection of plans as probable junk

indicators.note: rejection here means the word for plans is turned back

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Plans thrown out as likely rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolicited email is usually worthless, so spam is probable junk mail.

clue.text: Artist, a sizzler?

definitions.meaning: Francis ... was an Irish-born British painter
rashers of cured pork sizzle in a frying pan

explanation.surface: A painter who is hot stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter Francis shares the name with the breakfast meat that sizzles when fried.

clue.text: Caught breaking into it, keen criminal — one collared?

indicators.note: breaking into means the caught letter enters the rearranged letters
criminal means the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A keen criminal caught breaking in, one collared by police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' shuffles IT and KEEN into NEKTIE, which C enters.
explanation.definitionFit: This item is worn round the neck under a shirt collar, so it is one collared.

clue.text: Shakespearean bagging the hide

indicators.note: bagging means the king's name captures the other word

parts.note: King Lear is a Shakespeare tragic hero
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean actor bags himself an animal's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanned animal skin is called a hide, so hide is a near synonym.

clue.text: Powder keg's contents knocked over in style

indicators.note: knocked over means the pieces are turned backwards

parts.note: talc is a fine powder

indicators.note: contents picks the middle letter of keg's

explanation.surface: A powder keg's contents spilled out, with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with brilliance or panache is doing it with style.

clue.text: Stir beyond two thirds of Russian sugar

indicators.note: beyond means the stir word comes after
two thirds of keeps six of the nine letters, dropping the last three

parts.note: a Muscovite is a Russian from Moscow
a stir is a fuss, an ado

explanation.surface: Stirring sugar into most of a Russian's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an unrefined brown cane sugar with a strong molasses flavour.
